title: Observability of Hawking radiation
bottleneck: Hawking radiation from astrophysical black holes is far too faint and cold to detect, with a solar-mass black hole radiating at a temperature a million times below the cosmic microwave background. All experimental evidence comes from analogue systems like flowing Bose-Einstein condensates, which mimic the mathematics but may not share the underlying physics.
why_it_blocks: Hawking radiation is the single most important prediction at the quantum-gravity interface; if it can never be observed even in principle for real black holes, a cornerstone of the field rests on untestable calculation.
current_state: Analogue experiments have measured stimulated and spontaneous Hawking-like emission with thermal spectra, and primordial black holes evaporating today would give gamma-ray signals that are actively searched for but not found.
